item.title: Agnico Eagle has no plans to join Barrick’s IPO
item.description: Agnico CEO Ammar Al-Joundi says its own growth strategy leaves little reason to invest in Barrick’s planned gold spinoff.
item.dc:creator: Marina Meireles
item.content:encoded:
Agnico Eagle has no plans to join Barrick’s IPO

Marina Meireles | September 15, 2026 | 11:26 am Exploration   Markets   Top Companies   Canada   USA   Gold

( Image courtesy of Barrick Mining. )

Agnico Eagle (TSX, NYSE: AEM), one of the world’s three largest gold producers, has no interest in participating in Barrick Mining’s (TSX: ABX), (NYSE: B) proposed North American initial public offering (IPO), CEO Ammar Al-Joundi said.

“It would not make sense for us to buy into their North America IPO,” Al-Joundi said in an interview with Reuters.

“Strategically we have our own business and it is looking pretty good,” he said, adding that it is not a question of valuation or whether it is a good deal or not. Al-Joundi said if Agnico Eagle attempted to acquire the Nevada assets of Barrick, it would be up to Barrick’s board and management to decide what they want moving forward, Reuters reported.

Barrick is pursuing the IPO to sharpen operational focus and unlock value from its North American portfolio. Analysts have viewed the plan as a potential catalyst for Barrick’s shares  after years of cost overruns and missed profit targets.

Shares in Agnico Eagle were slightly down 0.3% to C$273.73 apiece by mid-day Tuesday in Toronto, valuing the company at C$138.7 billion ($99 billion). Barrick Mining shares were up 0.28% to C$59.12 apiece, valuing the company at C$97.3 billion ($69 billion).

IPO prospects

Analysts at Jeffries said in 2025 a standalone company would appeal to major gold producers such as Newmont (NYSE, ASX: NEM) and Agnico Eagle. The company’s smaller size and lack of non-core assets in more challenging jurisdictions could make it easier to acquire than Barrick as a whole, they said.

The proposed company would centre on Barrick’s interests in Nevada Gold Mines and Pueblo Viejo, as well as its wholly owned Fourmile discovery in Nevada. The assets produced about 2 million attributable oz. of gold in 2025.

The assets will operate with standalone leadership and greater flexibility under the new structure, and separate the business from operations in more risky jurisdictions, including Mali and Pakistan, Barrick said.

Barrick names North America team ahead of IPO

The timing remains uncertain. Bloomberg reported in early September that Barrick was considering delaying its IPO plans until 2027 after previously targeting completion by the end of 2026.

(With files from Reuters and Bloomberg)

item.title: Radiant World sues Glencore for $2 billion
item.description: It escalates mounting legal scrutiny over allegedly falsified iron ore trades, invoices and financing involving the two trading firms.
item.dc:creator: Cecilia Jamasmie
item.content:encoded:
Radiant World sues Glencore for $2 billion

Staff Writer | September 15, 2026 | 5:03 am Regulatory Issues   Top Companies   Asia   Europe   USA   Iron Ore

Six Battery Road (brown building on left), hosts Radiant World headquarters in Singapore. ( Image: WikiMedia Commons. )

Radiant World and affiliated iron ore trader Sapphire Minmetals have filed a lawsuit against Swiss commodity trader and miner Glencore (LON: GLEN), in Singapore, claiming $2 billion in damages.

Radiant World and Sapphire Minmetals are subject to a London court order freezing up to $499 million in assets after a Jefferies-managed fund alleged they used fake iron ore invoices in a scheme to defraud it, Bloomberg reported on Tuesday, citing people familiar with the matter.

Radiant World also faces lawsuits in Singapore from trade-finance platform Incomlend and a unit of Japan’s Mizuho Financial Group. Incomlend is seeking more than $34 million over allegedly fraudulent Glencore contracts.

Glencore said Tuesday it had found evidence that Radiant World and associated companies sent several financial institutions falsified invoices and contracts as well as fabricated emails purportedly from Glencore employees.

The Swiss company noted it had incurred losses and been exposed to risks through its dealings with the companies and would pursue appropriate action.

Fleeing sinking ship

Since accusations against Radiant World became public, the company has lost nearly half its iron ore traders in China and Singapore, while staff have also departed its London and Geneva offices. Some employees were reportedly dismissed while others resigned. Sapphire Minmetals has also reduced staff in China and Singapore.

Jefferies fund wins Singapore asset freeze against Radiant World

Radiant World has previously denied wrongdoing and said it conducts its business according to the highest commercial and legal standards.

The dispute threatens what was once a sizeable commodity trading operation as lenders, counterparties and employees retreat. Major trading houses including Vitol Group, Cargill and Glencore moved to cut ties with Radiant World after concerns emerged in July over allegedly falsified documents provided to lenders.

Under scrutiny

Glencore, previously a major backer of the group, has taken a $480 million provision related to its exposure to Radiant World. Radiant World and Sapphire Minmetals have in turn claimed they suffered more than $2 billion in losses because of Glencore’s actions, which they are now hoping to get back.

Authorities have also scrutinized the company. The US Department of Justice, US Commodity Futures Trading Commission and Singapore police are investigating Radiant World, while Singapore authorities have raided its headquarters.

Radiant World sent lender fake Glencore deals, lawsuit says

The latest staffing reductions are the second round since July, when lenders began withdrawing credit lines and major commodity traders distanced themselves from Radiant World.

Among the departures is Leon Jin, a veteran trader who headed Radiant World’s iron ore business in China. Jin left in late August after the company encountered difficulties carrying out daily operations, Bloomberg reported.

Base metals traders Francois-Henri Audibert and Kelvin Li are also said to be leaving. Radiant World still has staff in its metals unit, which operated largely independently from the troubled iron ore division.

Sapphire Minmetals has cut two operations employees, one in Shanghai and another in Singapore, while retaining a small group of traders in Beijing to manage its remaining iron ore business.

Radiant World and Sapphire Minmetals are legally separate but closely related, leaving both exposed to the freezing order as their trading operations contract.

item.title: Glencore, Mercuria compete for Venezuela aluminum smelter deal
item.description: Trading giants are said to be exploring a deal that could revive Venalum after years of power shortages and underinvestment.
item.dc:creator: Marina Meireles
item.content:encoded:
Glencore, Mercuria compete for Venezuela aluminum smelter deal

Marina Meireles | September 11, 2026 | 9:50 am Markets   Europe   Latin America   Aluminum   Bauxite   Oil & Gas

Aluminum ore in various shapes. ( Stock image by vxnaghiyev. )

Mercuria Energy Group Ltd. and Glencore Plc (LON: GLEN) are two of the firms exploring a deal for Venalum, Venezuela’s largest aluminum smelter, that could help revive production after years of decline.

The potential agreement comes as Venezuela struggles to rebuild an industrial sector hampered by economic turmoil, power shortages and years of underinvestment, Bloomberg News reported, citing people familiar with the talks.

The structure of any agreement remains unclear, but discussions with the Venezuelan government have included taking over operations at the smelter and securing access to the aluminum it produces, according to Bloomberg .

Venezuela’s mining sector: more data needed on geological potential

Venalum, located in Puerto Ordaz near hydroelectric power resources and bauxite reserves, has the capacity to produce about 430,000 metric tons of primary aluminum annually. A deal could help restore the facility as a major producer following years of power shortages, economic difficulties and under-investment.

Strategic foothold

Glencore has a history of dealings with Venezuela’s state-owned aluminum industry, including providing financing to producers. A new agreement would deepen its involvement as the US seeks greater influence over Venezuela and its mineral and oil resources.

Mercuria is said to be partnering with Heeney Capital, a private mining investment firm, on the potential transaction. The companies have previously worked together on deals in Venezuela to gain access to the country’s commodities and metals.

US-Venezuela oil pact raises legal, transparency doubts

No agreement has been reached and the talks could still collapse, according to Bloomberg. Glencore, Mercuria, Heeney Capital and Venezuela’s Information Ministry did not comment.

(With files from Bloomberg )
